title: The Tree That Was Always There

brief.premise: An adult remembers childhood summers at his aunt's house in Nazreth (Adama), Ethiopia, where he, his sister and his cousin climbed a small, ordinary tree in the patio after breakfast, until one morning its branches had been cut off and only the stump remained.
brief.audience: A general audience watching a short, personal film.
brief.intent: Convey the quiet loss of an ordinary place that had become part of a childhood, without explaining why the tree was cut.

style: grounded, intimate cinematic realism, natural soft morning light, muted warm colours, gentle film grain, 35mm, shallow depth of field

character.name: The three children
character.description: Setting: the aunt's modest single-storey house in Nazreth (Adama), Ethiopia, with a small patio in front of it. When children appear they are always the same three Ethiopian children: the narrator, a boy of about twelve or thirteen; his sister, a girl; and their cousin, a boy; in simple everyday summer clothes, with natural, understated expressions

music.prompt: instrumental, warm, intimate, nostalgic, gently bittersweet, soft plucked acoustic strings, sparse soft piano, subtle airy textures, Ethiopian pentatonic phrasing, slow, spacious

choice.reason: Chosen from measured levels and spectrograms, not by listening (seed 1015): the only candidate whose shape follows the story, fuller early, a natural breath before the discovery at 49 s, sparse sustained notes through the loss, dissolving to silence by about 72 s. It ends about 4 s before the cut; to be confirmed by listening.
